package_info.why_malicious: The Carbanak malware, as adapted and deployed by FIN7, is designed to gain unauthorized administrative access to victim systems, exfiltrate payment card data, and facilitate large-scale financial theft. Its deployment is always for malicious purposes, including credential theft, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.

execution_context.file_location: malicious file attached to phishing email (e.g., .doc, .exe, .lnk)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious macro or executable payload (e.g., embedded in Office document or disguised executable) that, when opened, downloads and executes the Carbanak malware.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the attachment, the code executes a macro or drops an executable, which downloads and runs the Carbanak malware, establishing persistence and command-and-control (C2) communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected macros or executables in email attachments that initiate network connections and download further payloads are classic indicators of phishing and malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate business documents should not contain macros or executables that download and run additional software.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted internal workflows (rare, and with strict controls).
key_indicators: Presence of macros or embedded executables in email attachments
Network connections initiated immediately after opening document
Dropping and executing files in user directories

execution_context.file_location: installed malware binary on victim endpoint (e.g., C:\Users\Public\carbanak.exe)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Carbanak core module: establishes C2 channel, injects into system processes, enumerates and exfiltrates payment card data from POS software memory.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial execution, the malware establishes a C2 connection, injects itself into running processes, scans memory of POS applications for card data, and exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Memory scraping of POS software and exfiltration of sensitive data is a hallmark of POS malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate raw card data from memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging tools may access process memory, but never exfiltrate data.
key_indicators: Memory scraping for card data patterns (Track 1/2)

attack_chain.action: Phishing email with malicious attachment is sent to target; user is socially engineered to open the file.
Malicious macro or executable downloads and runs the Carbanak malware payload.
Carbanak malware establishes C2, injects into POS processes, scrapes memory for card data.
Exfiltrated card data is sent to attacker-controlled servers for monetization.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sale of stolen card data on underground markets

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected macro or executable execution from email attachments
Network connections to known C2 infrastructure after document open
Process injection into POS or financial software
Memory scraping for card data patterns (Track 1/2 data)
Exfiltration of large volumes of data to external servers
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros received via email
Unknown executables dropped in user or public directories
Malware binaries named to mimic legitimate software (e.g., carbanak.exe, pos.exe)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains/IPs associated with Carbanak/FIN7 C2
Unusual HTTPS or HTTP POST requests after document open
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of macros or unknown executables from email attachments, especially those that initiate outbound network connections. Detect process injection and memory scraping behaviors targeting POS software. Use threat intelligence to block known C2 domains/IPs. Alert on exfiltration of card data patterns and large outbound data transfers from POS systems.
